nodes.label: ensure-ffmpeg-addon Build Step
nodes.rationale: scripts/ensure-ffmpeg-addon.mjs builds @theia/ffmpeg's native addon before theia build so an install that skipped dependency scripts does not fail on Cannot find module '../build/Debug/ffmpeg.node'.

nodes.label: @theia/ffmpeg Native Addon
nodes.rationale: Theia's Electron build needs @theia/ffmpeg's node-gyp addon, which the install script normally builds; electron-app's native:ffmpeg step now builds it when missing.

nodes.label: Host Factory Lifetime
nodes.rationale: Capability factories live in the workspace extension's frontend module for the host's whole lifetime, so a restored terminal is restorable after the plugin that exposed it is disabled.

nodes.label: Host-Owned Capability Panels
nodes.rationale: Instances created through a host capability are host-owned: WorkspacePanelRegistry.isHostPanelType marks them, they stay open, and plugin disablement never destroys them.

nodes.label: Host Owns Capability Factories and Their Panels
nodes.norm_label: host owns capability factories and their panels
nodes.rationale: A capability factory is contributed by the host's Theia integration and lives for the host's lifetime; plugins may only request panels, so a running terminal survives its plugin's disablement.

nodes.label: Trust and Enabled State Store
nodes.rationale: Trust and enabled state persist in ~/.icebox/plugins.json, overridable with $ICEBOX_STATE_DIR.

nodes.label: Curated Host Panel Capabilities
nodes.rationale: Native host functionality reaches plugins only through curated capability ids such as icebox.terminal; the DI container, WidgetManager, host services, raw widgets and a general widget factory are never exposed.

nodes.label: Host Panel Capability Contract
nodes.rationale: HOST_PANEL_CAPABILITIES and HostPanelRegistration let a plugin adopt a curated host capability through api.panels.registerHostPanel instead of importing Theia internals.

nodes.label: Adopting a Host Capability
nodes.rationale: registerHostPanel({id, title, capabilityId}) requests a host-built panel, hasHostCapability gates whether the build exposes it, and a capability id is a stable contract rather than an import path.

nodes.label: Host Panel Capability Catalog
nodes.rationale: HostPanelFactoryRegistry is a curated catalog of native panels named by stable ids such as icebox.terminal, contributed through Inversify and reachable only via api.panels.registerHostPanel.

nodes.label: icebox.terminal Host Factory
nodes.rationale: TerminalHostPanelFactory creates a real terminal widget through TerminalFrontendContribution.newTerminal() and returns the widget itself so TerminalService, splits and Theia's restore keep working.

nodes.label: Never Bundle Theia Internals to Fake Host UI
nodes.norm_label: never bundle theia internals to fake host ui
nodes.rationale: Bundling @theia/* or xterm into a plugin produces duplicate containers and widgets the shell cannot adopt, and the bundler allowlist will not link them.

nodes.label: Terminal Placement Override
nodes.rationale: CanvasTerminalShellHandler forces area 'main' and CanvasTerminalFrontendContribution turns initializeLayout into a no-op, because @theia/terminal sends panel terminals to a bottom area the canvas does not have.

nodes.label: One Host Code Path per Panel Kind
nodes.norm_label: one host code path per panel kind
nodes.rationale: Every path that opens the same kind of native panel must use the same host code, so no built-in command points at a region the canvas does not have.

nodes.label: Host-Published Workspace Services
nodes.rationale: workspace.resources turns absolute paths into stable URIs with stat and list, and workspace.selection carries {uri, ranges} plus change notifications mirrored onto workspace/selection-changed.

nodes.label: No Prescribed Dock Placement
nodes.rationale: Plugin registration never prescribes a dock location; only the user or an explicit user action chooses placement.

nodes.label: Plugin-First Desktop Workspace
nodes.rationale: Icebox is a plugin-first desktop workspace, not an IDE with a fixed layout; the initial workspace is an empty full-window docking canvas.

nodes.label: Repository Layout
nodes.rationale: workspace-core, packages/plugin-api, packages/plugin-runtime, packages/plugin-build, packages/ui-kit, plugins/ and the electron-app/browser-app targets each own one concern.

nodes.label: Theia 1.77.0 Version Pin
nodes.rationale: The application is pinned to Theia 1.77.0 with Cordis as the native-plugin lifecycle engine.

nodes.label: Canvas Shell Layout
nodes.rationale: The extension replaces the standard IDE shell layout with one full-window main DockPanel and no predefined left, right or bottom regions.

nodes.label: Main DockPanel Shell
nodes.rationale: Theia's ApplicationShell mainPanel is already a multiple-document TheiaDockPanel, so the extension changes the root shell layout instead of adding another docking engine.

nodes.label: Empty Docking Canvas Goal
nodes.rationale: No editor, sidebar, terminal, chat, file tree, Git view or toolbar opens by default; users choose which panels to open and arrange them.

nodes.label: Never Prescribe Panel Placement
nodes.rationale: activate registers panel types and commands and must not open panels; only a user action opens one.

nodes.label: Plugin Loading Flow
nodes.rationale: Discover plugin.json, validate id/version/apiVersion/entrypoints/dependencies, resolve Cordis dependencies, import the frontend ESM bundle into the renderer and the backend ESM bundle into the Node backend, adapt activate(api) into a Cordis Fiber, and dispose it on disable or uninstall.

nodes.label: Plugin Discovery Order
nodes.rationale: Startup scans $ICEBOX_PLUGINS_DIR, <appPath>/../plugins, <appPath>/plugins and ~/.icebox/plugins in order, and problems surface as plugin manager diagnostics instead of blocking startup.

nodes.label: Strict Manifest Validation
nodes.rationale: Ids are namespaced and globally unique, versions semver, apiVersion must equal the host's version, entrypoints stay inside the folder, and dependencies must resolve before any import.

nodes.label: Plugin Manifest Fields
nodes.rationale: plugin.json declares id, name, version, apiVersion, entrypoints, dependencies and contributes; entrypoints stay inside the plugin folder and point at .js/.mjs bundles.

nodes.label: Plugin Folder Structure
nodes.rationale: plugins/<plugin-id>/ holds plugin.json, package.json, src/frontend and src/backend entrypoints and git-ignored dist bundles.

nodes.label: Automatic Plugin Discovery
nodes.rationale: The backend scans the built-in plugins/ folder and ~/.icebox/plugins and validates every plugin.json before importing anything.

nodes.label: Automatic Panel Closure on Unload
nodes.rationale: Every panel instance goes through one host WidgetManager factory, so panels are tracked by owner and persisted by Theia's layout restorer; a plugin unload closes the panels it opened.

nodes.label: Writing a Plugin Entry Point
nodes.rationale: Each plugin folder has a plugin.json plus src/frontend and/or src/backend entrypoints and builds with the plugin bundler; plugins/README.md is the authoring guide.

nodes.label: Implemented Plugin Runtime
nodes.rationale: The runtime is implemented end to end: discovery, frontend ESM loading, Cordis activation and disposal, panel ownership plus layout persistence, shared services/events over RPC, and the plugin manager trust warning.

nodes.label: Third-Party Plugin Trust Gate
nodes.rationale: Any plugin discovered under ~/.icebox/plugins is third-party code with full system access and stays disabled until the user accepts the confirmation dialog.

nodes.label: Plugin Build Tooling
nodes.rationale: node packages/plugin-build/build.mjs <pluginDir> (or npm run build:plugins) bundles each plugin's entrypoints.

nodes.label: Third-Party Trust Confirmation
nodes.rationale: Third-party plugins require an explicit full-system-access confirmation before activation while built-in plugins are trusted by shipping with the app.

nodes.label: Plugin Manager Panel Styling
nodes.rationale: Layout lives in plugin-manager-styles.ts: one gutter, one row rhythm, a text column for name, id@version, badges and description, and a right-pinned action group with fixed button width.

nodes.label: Full System Access Trust Model
nodes.rationale: All plugins are trusted native code running in the Theia renderer and Node backend with no iframe, VM, worker, subprocess or restricted mode.

nodes.label: Trust Warning Is Disclosure, Not a Boundary
nodes.norm_label: trust warning is disclosure, not a boundary
nodes.rationale: The install/enable warning makes full system access explicit and requires a trust decision, but the only execution split is Theia's ordinary frontend/backend architecture.

nodes.label: Self-Contained Backend Bundle
nodes.rationale: Backend bundles are self-contained ESM so a user-installed plugin in ~/.icebox/plugins does not depend on the app's node_modules layout; electron stays external.

nodes.label: Cordis Does Not Sandbox
nodes.rationale: Cordis manages lifecycle and dependencies; it does not sandbox plugins or guarantee that ESM module records are removed from memory after disposal.

nodes.label: Theme With Host CSS Variables
nodes.rationale: The dark theme means hardcoded light colors are a bug; style with --theia-* variables and use codicon glyphs instead of bundled icon assets.

nodes.label: Plugins Are Trusted Native Code
nodes.rationale: Frontend code runs in the normal Theia renderer and backend code in the normal Node process with full filesystem, process and network access.

nodes.label: Trust Shown as a Badge
nodes.rationale: Rows report trust as a badge because trust is granted by the confirmation dialog the first enable opens; a toggle that could only revoke it would be a trap.

nodes.label: Theia RPC Boundary
nodes.rationale: Frontend and backend plugins cross Theia's existing RPC boundary; a renderer plugin reaches a backend service through api.services.remote instead of opening its own channel.

nodes.label: Services and Typed Events
nodes.rationale: Services carry callable capabilities and durable shared state, typed events carry notifications, and cross-plugin data contracts live in plugin-api with stable ids and URI-based resource identities.

nodes.label: Reserved Service and Event Ids
nodes.rationale: git.repository, agent.sessions and git/changes-updated are reserved ids feature plugins fill in; they are frozen so plugins can code against them now.

nodes.label: URI-Based Resource Contracts
nodes.rationale: ResourceUri, ResourceSelection, ResourceStat and the workspace resources/selection services are the cross-plugin data contracts, with ServiceRegistryAPI.remote bridging renderer to backend over Theia's RPC channel.

nodes.label: Versioned Plugin Contracts
nodes.rationale: The package exposes versioned contracts shared by the host and native plugins: panels, commands, ui, services, events, origin and onDispose on both API surfaces.

nodes.label: Compiled @icebox Types Before TypeScript Runs
nodes.rationale: The @icebox/* workspace packages are not published and their lib/ output is not committed, so npm run build:workspace-core is required after an --ignore-scripts install.

nodes.label: Stable Service and Event Ids
nodes.rationale: Use WORKSPACE_SERVICE_IDS and WORKSPACE_EVENT_IDS from plugin-api, never duplicate ids, and call remote<T>() for a backend service because it throws in backend code.

nodes.label: Typecheck Command for Plugin Sources
nodes.rationale: The bundler does not typecheck, so run tsc --noEmit over the plugin sources before committing.

nodes.label: Postinstall Ordered Package Build
nodes.rationale: npm ci/npm install runs the root postinstall, which compiles @icebox/plugin-api, @icebox/plugin-runtime and workspace-core in order because their lib/ output is not committed.

nodes.label: Manual build:workspace-core Fallback
nodes.rationale: An install that used --ignore-scripts must run npm run build:workspace-core once by hand or TypeScript reports TS2307 on @icebox/plugin-api.

nodes.label: Build Order Direction
nodes.rationale: Build stable manifest and API contracts, the Cordis runtime and ESM loading, panel ownership and disposal, the service/event registry, settings and plugin manager, then the real terminal, agent-chat, file-browser and Git plugins.

nodes.label: API Version Compatibility Policy
nodes.rationale: Additive API changes are preferred; breaking changes require an apiVersion change plus an explicit compatibility policy, and the package stays independent of Cordis internals.

nodes.label: Keep Frontend and Backend Split
nodes.rationale: Node APIs are only allowed in src/backend, so the renderer bundle stays loadable in the browser target.

nodes.label: No Cross-Plugin Imports
nodes.rationale: Plugins communicate through services and events only, so no plugin imports another plugin's implementation.

nodes.label: Plugin Bundle Delivery Paths
nodes.rationale: The browser target fetches served bundles under PLUGIN_ASSET_PREFIX while the Electron file:// origin carries the bundle over the RPC channel via readFrontendBundle, since the asset route sends no CORS headers.

nodes.label: Bundled Feature Plugins
nodes.rationale: File Browser, Git, Agent Chat and Terminal each pair a frontend panel with an optional backend service.

nodes.label: Adopting the Host Terminal Capability
nodes.rationale: The Terminal plugin adopts icebox.terminal through api.panels.registerHostPanel, so its bundle contains no Theia or xterm code and creation, persistence and disposal stay host-owned.

nodes.label: Host Module Allowlist
nodes.rationale: react, react-dom, the Lumino packages and selected @theia/core entrypoints stay external and are rewritten to the host's instances; the canonical list lives in plugin-host-protocol.ts.

nodes.label: Panel Host Tools
nodes.rationale: createWidget receives (instanceId, host) where host.React, host.widgets and host.createReactWidget are the host's own instances, so plugin widgets are the same classes the shell docks.

nodes.label: Panel Disposal on Unload
nodes.rationale: Unloading a plugin removes exactly its own registrations and closes every panel instance it opened.

nodes.label: Plugin Runtime Contract
nodes.rationale: activate(api) receives a typed FrontendPluginAPI or BackendPluginAPI and everything registered through it is owned by the plugin and disposed on unload.

nodes.label: Frontend ESM Bundle Loading
nodes.rationale: Frontend bundles are served by the backend for the browser target or handed over the RPC channel for a file:// Electron origin, then dynamically imported.

nodes.label: Shared Host Module Resolution
nodes.rationale: Shared host modules such as react, @lumino/widgets and Theia browser/common resolve to the host's own instances so plugin widgets are real Lumino widgets.

nodes.label: Workspace Docking Service
nodes.rationale: WorkspaceDockingService.openPanel opens a registered panel with split/tab modes relative to an existing widget.

nodes.label: Workspace Panel Registry
nodes.rationale: WorkspacePanelRegistry holds panel definitions registered by plugins and by other Theia extensions, and every instance is created through one host WidgetFactory so WidgetManager owns them.

nodes.label: No Default Panel Placement
nodes.rationale: A panel definition does not specify a region or default position; extensions register capabilities and the user controls the arrangement.

nodes.label: Backend Entry Must Be src/backend/index.ts
nodes.rationale: The bundler only detects src/backend/index.ts, not .tsx or .mts, so the backend entry must stay at that exact path.

nodes.label: Plugin Folder Layout
nodes.rationale: plugin.json is the manifest and source of truth, src/frontend/index.tsx and src/backend/index.ts are the entries, dist/ holds git-ignored ESM bundles.

nodes.label: Scaffold Feature Plugins
nodes.rationale: Each child folder of plugins/ is a self-contained feature package owning its manifest, metadata, sources, assets and built bundles.

nodes.label: No Test-Only or Demo Plugins
nodes.rationale: Early plugins must implement real basic functionality, and the host ships no demo panels, demo commands or placeholder widgets.

nodes.label: Build Real Functionality, No Demos
nodes.rationale: No test-only, placeholder or demo plugins; a scaffold must exercise the real contract and then be completed.

nodes.label: Rule Zero: Self-Contained Plugin Folder
nodes.rationale: A plugin is one self-contained folder; never edit workspace-core, packages or the app targets to add a plugin, and report a missing runtime capability instead of patching the host.

nodes.label: Cordis-Managed Plugin Fiber
nodes.rationale: Each module's activate(api) is adapted into a Cordis-managed plugin Fiber, and contributions are registered through disposable effects.

nodes.label: ESM Module Cache and Code-Unload Limits
nodes.norm_label: esm module cache and code-unload limits
nodes.rationale: Cordis disposal cleans plugin resources but native ESM module records may stay cached, so true code-unload or in-place binary replacement must not be promised.

nodes.label: Panel Ownership and Disposal
nodes.rationale: Unloading a plugin closes every panel instance it owns and withdraws its services, events and commands; resources the host created through a host panel capability stay host-owned.

nodes.label: Exactly One Restoration Owner per Widget
nodes.norm_label: exactly one restoration owner per widget
nodes.rationale: The workspace plugin-panel mechanism restores plugin-built panels and the original Theia factory restores host-capability panels; never register the same widget under both.

nodes.label: activate(api) Runtime Contract
nodes.rationale: Everything registered through api belongs to the plugin and is disposed on unload, and returning a disposer from activate is optional.

nodes.label: Single Restoration Authority
nodes.rationale: Plugin-built panels are registered under icebox.workspace.panel and restored by the workspace mechanism, host-capability panels only under their original Theia factory, so persistence and ownership can never disagree.

nodes.label: Reload or Restart for Unreplaceable Modules
nodes.norm_label: reload or restart for unreplaceable modules
nodes.rationale: When a module cannot be replaced safely the answer is application reload or restart, not in-place module surgery.

nodes.label: Dispose Everything You Start
nodes.rationale: Watchers, timers, processes and listeners go through onDispose or returned disposers because Cordis tears down the fiber but cannot see raw Node handles.

nodes.label: No Layout Ownership Marker for Host Panels
nodes.norm_label: no layout ownership marker for host panels
nodes.rationale: A layout-level ownership marker is only worthwhile for panels whose UI and lifecycle genuinely belong to a plugin; host-capability panels deliberately have none.

nodes.label: Never Promise Code Unload
nodes.rationale: Native ESM module records may stay cached, so reload or restart is the answer when a module cannot be replaced safely.

nodes.label: Independent Layout Persistence
nodes.rationale: User layouts are persisted independently of plugin installation and the startup canvas stays empty unless the user explicitly restores a saved layout.

nodes.label: Per-Instance Panel State Contract
nodes.rationale: PanelOpenOptions.state is a plain JSON object owned by one panel instance; the host stores it with the layout and passes it back to createWidget after a restart.

nodes.label: Per-Instance Panel State
nodes.rationale: open(panelId, {state}) carries a plain JSON object that survives save/restore and comes back to createWidget, so per-tab data never lives in plugin-level state.

nodes.label: One Agent Session per Chat Tab
nodes.norm_label: one agent session per chat tab
nodes.rationale: The backend keys each agent process and transcript by panel instance id and the agent travels in the panel state, so restoring a layout restores the tabs.

nodes.label: Agent Wire Protocols (ACP and pi-rpc)
nodes.rationale: Agent Chat supports the Agent Client Protocol over stdio and Pi's own JSONL command/event protocol, because Pi has no ACP mode.

nodes.label: Layout and Instance-State Persistence
nodes.rationale: Theia's ShellLayoutRestorer saves the main DockPanel layout plus per-instance panel state so splits, tabs, sizes, last active panel and each tab's JSON state survive a restart.

nodes.label: Unavailable Panel Placeholder
nodes.rationale: A saved layout for a disabled or uninstalled plugin restores an unavailable placeholder instead of failing the whole layout, and re-enabling the plugin brings the real panel back.

nodes.label: One Panel Instance, One Session
nodes.rationale: A panel that owns a process, connection or transcript keys it by instance id, so a second tab never disturbs the first.

nodes.label: Tool Entrypoints Invoked Through node
nodes.rationale: Install and build scripts call node node_modules/@theia/cli/bin/theia.js instead of the node_modules/.bin wrappers, whose .cmd %_prog% line breaks where node is itself a shim.

nodes.label: node Instead of .bin Wrappers in Scripts
nodes.norm_label: node instead of .bin wrappers in scripts
nodes.rationale: node_modules/.bin wrappers are .cmd files on Windows whose quoted %_prog% fails where node is a shim, aborting npm install, so scripts call node directly.

nodes.label: Browser Target Port and Hostname Flags
nodes.norm_label: browser target port and hostname flags
nodes.rationale: npm run start:browser forwards arguments after -- to Theia's start command, and the listen address uses Theia's --hostname flag; there is no --host.
